hitl_conditions: Human review when classification confidence is below a predefined threshold (e.g., <0.85); technicians validate/correct predicted fault type during interventions (active learning); operator verification tolerated for mobile equipment; crews intensify inspections within ~200 cycles of predicted end-of-life.
key_finding: Three-layer IoT-digital twin-ML architecture for predictive maintenance of distribution-centre equipment (forklifts, conveyors, AGVs): ensemble anomaly detection (F1 0.915), LSTM/RF RUL prediction (R2 0.907), fault classification (92.1%); reported 42% less unplanned downtime and 4.5-month payback; low-confidence predictions routed to technicians, whose corrections retrain models.

quotes.text: The DT in this paper is considered as a time-dependent multi-physics mapping. This DT is based on the Data-Model-Fusion (DMF) principle rather than on a static model.
quotes.section: Research methodology - Digital twin model construction

quotes.text: The predictive maintenance solution was tested in a 12-month pilot for a midsize distribution center with 150 pieces of equipment, such as conveyors, forklifts, AGVs, and sorting systems.

For anomaly detection, Remaining Unit Life (RUL) prediction, and failure classification, this study utilized Isolation Forest (iForest), Autoencoders, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Random Forest (RF) machine learning models.

The system includes HITL (Human-in-the-Loop) validation via real-time dashboards. When the ML layer produces a class with a confidence score lower than a predefined threshold (e.g., < 0.85), the event is flagged for manual analysis.
Prediction is validated as maintenance teams validate or correct the predicted fault type during intervention. This feedback enriches the classification model in an active learning fashion

The implementation simulates sensor data and does not rely on any external datasets. All data for the digital twin system are generated dynamically within the SensorNetwork class using predefined baseline values combined with controlled random variations
